cells.tense: You're here at the middle of it, asking real questions and letting the answers change what you do next.
cells.ask: Take one thing you understand well and teach it to somebody just starting — plainly, out loud, without dressing it up.
cells.core: You're curious the way a person is when it counts — you listen for what's actually true instead of what you expected to hear, and what you notice holds up when you act on it. Knowing you can't explain yet doesn't rattle you; you sit with it and let it work. That quiet accuracy is still forming, and it wants the next step: explaining it. Not defending it, not dressing it up — handing it over so somebody else can use it.\n\nTake one thing you understand well and teach it to somebody just starting. Out loud. Plainly. The last piece isn't required first — saying the part already in hand and letting the gap show is the whole move. What gets said comes back cleaner than it went out.
cells.sheetLine: You ask, you listen, and what you find holds — now say it out loud to somebody else.

cells.tense: You're living a few steps ahead of where you actually are, reaching for the version of this that finally makes sense.
cells.ask: Leave one thing genuinely undecided this week — not explained, not pinned down, just actually open.
cells.core: You're asking so far ahead that the questions have stopped touching anything real. Every conversation gets turned toward proving you've got it, every idea gets tested before it's had a chance to form, and the searching has become the point instead of the finding. The trouble isn't the curiosity — it's that you're bracing against not knowing instead of letting it be true for a while.\n\nLeave one thing genuinely undecided this week. Not explained, not pinned down — just open. The space doesn't have to be filled with answers. The knowing you're looking for shows up on its own when the forcing stops, and what you actually want to be pointed at gets clearer in the quiet.
cells.sheetLine: You're searching so hard that the answers can't land — let one thing stay open.

cells.tense: You're still standing where you stopped asking, and the questions you once carried have gone quiet beside you.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you're actually drawn toward right now — the thing you've stopped saying out loud — and let it surprise you on the way out.
cells.core: The pull toward something real is still there, but the voice that used to turn it over has stopped speaking up. You watch what's going on around you without letting it reach you, and the direction you'd move in stays somewhere behind the door you've stopped opening. It isn't that you have nothing to know — it's that you've gone quiet about what you know.\n\nTell one person what you're actually drawn toward right now, the thing you've stopped saying out loud. Not a plan, not a conviction — just the pull, as it feels today. Say it before it's formed and let the saying itself remind you what wanting feels like. That gets the current moving again, and the questions come back with it.
cells.sheetLine: You know more than you're saying — tell one person what you're drawn toward.

cells.tense: You're already moving toward what you want, but you talk about it as if the pull were a fact and you're just following it.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're drawn toward and finish the sentence with "because it was chosen" — say it once to someone who'd notice.
cells.core: You're already steering by something — you know which way you lean on the questions that matter, and real choices get made about what you give your attention to. But it gets described as though the direction were given, as if you were only reading it off a map someone else drew. You've been deciding and calling it discovery.\n\nName one thing you're drawn toward, and finish the sentence with: because it was chosen. Say it once to someone who'd notice. The preference was yours the whole time — the saying so is the only thing that's been missing, and it's the part only you can do.
cells.sheetLine: You've been choosing this all along — say it like it's yours.
